System specs

What it runs on

Windows and a DirectX 12 graphics card. The physics runs on the server, so the game's work is drawing.

MinimumRecommended
SystemWindows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x64)Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (x64)
GraphicsA DirectX 12 GPU; integrated graphics start on the Low preset (untested)A discrete DirectX 12 GPU
Memory16 GB16 GB
Disk4 GB free (the game is about 1.6 GB unpacked)4 GB free
ControlsA keyboard or a gamepadA DirectInput wheel and pedals
Measured

How it runs

RTX 3080 · 1920×1080

A 12-car GT3 race replayed by the built-in benchmark: about 105 fps on average, with 99% of frames under 12.1 ms.

The physics

One car's step takes about 2.4 µs on one core, and a whole 8-car tick (physics, AI, collisions, timing) about 40 µs, under 2% of the time a 420 Hz tick allows.

No software rendering

The game draws through the GPU; there is no CPU rendering fallback.

Upscaling

TSR everywhere; DLSS on NVIDIA RTX cards; FSR, with FSR 4's machine-learning upscaler on Radeon RX 7000 and 9000.

Displays

One screen or three (triple screens with bezel and angle correction), HDR output, and colour-vision palettes for the HUD.

Input

DirectInput wheels, pedals and button boxes with force feedback and per-wheelbase profiles; gamepads with rumble; keyboard.

Not supported

macOS, Linux and Windows on Arm for the game; VR headsets.

Hosting

Running a server

Where it runs

Windows, or Linux in Docker. The launcher can also start one beside the game.

Ports

9000/TCP for the lobby and 9001/UDP for telemetry and input, open to your players.

Content

The same cars and circuits as the players; a checksum warns anyone racing on different files.

From source

Building it yourself

Windows with Unreal Engine 5.8, Rust and Python 3 (numpy, Pillow, PyYAML). The Assetto Corsa importers need Python 3.11 or newer.

The build guide →
In active development

Get on the grid

Download the release, unzip it and run launcher.exe. It starts the game, with a local server if you want one.
